messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Hindi, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Hindi line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑by‑Word Mapping Table (Source → Hindi)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (truth‑condition) | Target Word / Phrase (Hindi) | Back‑Translation (English) | Status | |-------------|------------------------------------------|------------------------------|-----------------------------|--------| | **In** | locative “in” (all parts) | **में** | in | OK | | **tutte** | universal quantifier “all” | **सभी** | all | OK | | **parti** | set of “parts” of the world | **भागों** | parts | OK | | **impera** | “governs” each part | **शासन करता है** | governs | OK | | **e** | coordinating “and” | **और** | and | OK | | **quivi** (1st) | locative “there” (place of reign) | **वहीं** | there | OK | | **regge** | “reigns” at that place | **राज करता है** | reigns | OK | | **quivi** (2nd) | locative “there” (place of city/seat) | **वहां** | there | OK | | **è** | copular “is” (existence) | **है** | is | OK | | **la** | definite article (fem.) – not lexical in Hindi | — | (none) | **UNNECESSARY** | | **sua** | possessive “His” | **उसकी** | his | OK | | **città** | noun “city” | **नगरी** | city | OK | | **e** | coordinating “and” | **और** | and | OK | | **l’** | definite article (masc.) – not lexical in Hindi | — | (none) | **UNNECESSARY** | | **alto** | adjective “lofty” | **ऊँचा** | lofty | OK | | **seggio** | noun “seat” (throne) | **सिंहासन** | seat | OK | | **oh** | interjection “O” (vocative) | **हे** | O | OK | | **felice** | adjective “happy” (state of the chosen) | **धन्य** | blessed/happy | OK | | **colui** | pronoun “he” (the one elected) | **वह** | he | OK | | **cu’** | relative pronoun “whom” | **जिसे** | whom | OK | | **ivi** | locative “there/thereto” (place of election) | **वहां** | there | OK | | **elegge** | verb “elects” | **चुनता है** | elects | OK |
---
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: `la`, `l’` – Italian definite articles have no direct equivalents in Hindi and are naturally omitted. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** issues were detected.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Hindi script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Hindi text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line 127** - **Original:** सभी भागों में वह शासन करता है और वहीं वह राज करता है; - **Issue:** none - **Corrected:** no change
- **Line 128** - **Original:** वहां उसकी नगरी और उसका ऊँचा सिंहासन है: - **Issue:** none - **Corrected:** no change
